q: Explain the Save Layout button and its right-click menu.
a: It saves the current page's arrangement (tabs you dragged, gutters you resized, what you changed with the toolbar) as that page's layout. The page opens this way from now on, also after a restart, and the status line names the page it saved. Same as Window ▸ Workspaces ▸ **Save Changes to this Workspace** (`window.workspace.saveChanges`). Its right-click menu holds **Reset to Saved Layout**, **Restore Original Layout**, **Save Layout as Preset…** and **Manage Layout Presets…**.

q: A panel vanished from my Media page after some dragging. Get the page back the way I last saved it.
a:
1. Right-click **Save Layout** at the bottom right (left of Lessons).
2. Choose **Reset to Saved Layout** (also Window ▸ Workspaces ▸ Reset to Saved Layout, `window.workspace.reset`). The page goes back to your last saved arrangement.
3. Want the page as Revolution ships it instead? **Restore Original Layout** in the same menu (it also throws your saved version away).

q: Is Save Layout for one page or all of them?
a: One page: the page you are on. Each page has its own saved layout and its own Reset. To keep every page together under one name, save a **layout preset**: Window ▸ Layout Presets ▸ **Save Layout as Preset…** (`window.layoutPreset.save`).

q: Premiere has Window > Workspaces > Save Changes to this Workspace. Same thing here?
a: Yes: Window ▸ Workspaces ▸ **Save Changes to this Workspace** (`window.workspace.saveChanges`) and **Reset to Saved Layout** (`window.workspace.reset`) work as in Premiere. Revolution also puts them on the **Save Layout** button at the bottom right (left-click saves, right-click resets).

q: Resolve's Workspace menu has Layout Presets. Where's that?
a: Window ▸ **Layout Presets**: **Save Layout as Preset…** (`window.layoutPreset.save`), the saved presets by name to load (`window.layoutPreset.load`) and **Manage Layout Presets…** (`window.layoutPreset.manage`). The same two entries sit in the **Save Layout** button's right-click menu.

q: Make a layout preset called Laptop.
a:
1. Arrange the pages the way the laptop screen wants them.
2. Window ▸ Layout Presets ▸ **Save Layout as Preset…** (`window.layoutPreset.save`), or right-click **Save Layout** ▸ **Save Layout as Preset…**.
3. Type Laptop and confirm. From now on, choosing Laptop in Window ▸ Layout Presets brings every page back this way.

q: how do i rename or get rid of a layout preset
a: Window ▸ Layout Presets ▸ **Manage Layout Presets…** (`window.layoutPreset.manage`, or right-click **Save Layout** ▸ Manage Layout Presets…). The list lets you load, update, rename and delete each preset, and export or import one.

A layout preset exported to a file: **Manage Layout Presets…** ▸ **Export…** (`window.layoutPreset.export`) writes it, **Import…** (`window.layoutPreset.import`) reads one, for example from another computer. It holds every page's arrangement in that preset.

q: How do I throw away a page's saved changes from the menu?
a: Window ▸ Workspaces ▸ **Edit Workspaces…** lets you delete a page's saved changes (`window.workspace.delete`). The quicker way on the page itself: right-click **Save Layout** ▸ **Restore Original Layout**, which throws your saved version away and brings back the page as Revolution ships it.

q: Resolve workflow: what happens if I pick Fairlight Page under Window > Workspaces?
a: It opens the Fairlight page. In the Resolve workflow Window ▸ Workspaces lists the pages' workspaces (Media Page, Edit Page, Fairlight Page, Deliver Page, Color Grading), and choosing one of those names by command or key opens its page.

q: In the Resolve workflow, where does the Import mode take me?
a: To the Media page: in the Resolve workflow the Import mode (`mode.import`) opens the Media page.

q: Can I load a layout preset from the Save Layout button's menu?
a: Not directly: its right-click menu has **Save Layout as Preset…** and **Manage Layout Presets…**. Open Manage Layout Presets… and click **Load** next to the preset, or choose the preset's name in Window ▸ Layout Presets (`window.layoutPreset.load`).

q: Beginner here: do I need presets or is Save Layout enough?
a: There's no single right answer; it depends on how many setups you work in. **Save Layout** is enough for most: arrange the page, save, and use Reset when a panel goes missing. **Layout presets** pay off once you switch between very different setups (a laptop screen and a desk monitor, or cutting and finishing): one name brings back every page for that setup. Many people start with Save Layout and add a preset when a second screen or way of working comes along.

q: ok made a preset, how do I use it tomorrow
a: Choose its name in Window ▸ Layout Presets (`window.layoutPreset.load`). Every page takes the preset's arrangement and you land on the page it was saved on.

context.q: how do I save every page's layout under one name?
context.a: Window ▸ Layout Presets ▸ Save Layout as Preset… (`window.layoutPreset.save`), or right-click Save Layout ▸ Save Layout as Preset…, and give it a name.
